A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including material reorganized between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection, calibration, response-level correlation, uncertainty-aware decoding, and sample-count experiments across four LLMs and two datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds Llama-4 evaluations, grader and decomposition validation, threshold-transfer results, and aggregation comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 3.4 and 4.4 add minimum, geometric-mean, and rank-weighted response aggregation as evaluated alternatives. The decomposition procedures, four scorer families, and uncertainty-aware decoding rule remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 500 FactScore-Bio and 400 FactScore-STEM-Geo prompts. Appendix A.3 adds a cross-domain deployment scenario: thresholds calibrated on one dataset are applied to the other without target-domain calibration labels.

E2.justification: v2 adds normalized sequence probability as a white-box comparator alongside the four retained short-form black-box baselines in response-level evaluation. Tables 4 and 19–21 report this comparator for the original four LLMs; Llama-4 is excluded because its inference API did not expose log probabilities.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-4-Maverick-17B and substantial new evaluation protocols: 400 stratified units per grader-validation condition, manual assessment of 410 claims from 15 responses, and 50/50 calibration/test splits with F1-maximizing threshold searches. The original response-sampling budgets and main evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained sample-count ablations, v2 adds alternate-grader robustness, manual decomposition validation, cross-dataset and cross-scorer threshold transfer, and aggregation sensitivity analysis (Appendix A.1–A.3 and Section 4.4). These substantially expand checks on measurement reliability and deployment behavior.

E5.justification: Table 6 newly reports chance-corrected inter-grader agreement using Cohen's kappa. Neither version reports repeated-run seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the main performance comparisons; the existing descriptive plus/minus reporting convention is retained.

E6.justification: The shared four-model classification/calibration entries and Bio correlations are unchanged. v2 adds Llama-4 results, STEM-Geo response correlations, and validation/transfer outcomes. Examples include Llama-4 Bio claim-response AUROC of 0.791, grader kappa of 0.63–0.84, and decomposition faithfulness of 409/410. The new STEM-Geo correlations reveal different scorer rankings from Bio.

T1.justification: Table 22 explicitly defines the claim-diversity ratio as N_m-union/N_claim; v1 only states the approximate count relationship in its computational-cost discussion. This is a limited measurement-definition addition. The formal scorer equations, centrality definitions, and UAD rule are retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central taxonomy and headline findings about claim-response entailment, claim-level scoring, and UAD remain unchanged. v2 foregrounds FactScore-STEM-Geo in the abstract and introduction, but v1 already identifies it as the authors' new dataset in Section 4.1. The fifth model expands supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 develops the explanation of claim-QA failures through ambiguous or answer-revealing questions, interprets domain-dependent aggregation behavior, and discusses threshold portability. It also adds substantive limitations concerning intermediate granularities, reasoning budgets, Wikipedia topic-selection bias, and over-reliance on filtered UAD outputs.

D1.justification: v2 specifies a single NVIDIA T4 GPU for the retained runtime measurements, explains unavailable Llama-4 log probabilities, quantifies matched-claim comparison costs, and documents UAD implementation outputs. These are additional disclosures; the dataset-construction code and all eight prompt templates are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Nikitin et al. on kernel language entropy and Bai et al. on LongBench v2. New Table 2 clarifies which existing scorer configurations reproduce, generalize, or extend prior work. Numerous other reference changes update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the original wording are retained. v2 makes local language corrections, expands discussion passages, organizes Appendices A and B into named subsections, and updates publication, contact, contribution, and employment disclosures.

P2.justification: v2 adds novelty and validation/transfer tables, converts four rotated classification/calibration tables into eight upright tables, and substantially rearranges Figures 5 and 13 into aligned five-model panels. UAD and sample-count plots gain Llama-4 panels. The workflow figures and calibration Figure 14 are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 relies on unvalidated grading and decomposition and reports response-level correlations only for Bio. v2 adds alternate-grader and manual checks, completes the STEM-Geo response-level comparison, and tests aggregation and threshold portability. These additions materially strengthen the evaluation and clarify applicability limits. The small 15-response manual audit and remaining narrative/table ranking inconsistencies limit the conclusions, but the overall gains in evidential support and usability are substantial.
